chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ibn Bukayr, from Isma'il ibn Al-Hasan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, the one in Ihram, when he marries while being in Ihram, separation is effected between the two of them, then they do not remarry each other ever.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ritual consecration or state of sanctity for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.فُرِّقَ: Separation was effected / divorce was pronounced
key_terms.يَتَعَاوَدَانِ: They remarry each other / exchange marriage contracts

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a marriage contract performed while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies that while the marriage contract remains valid during Ihram, it is subject to dissolution (firq) rather than being void ab initio. The key scholarly implication is the prohibition of 'ta'addud' (remarriage) between the same couple, distinguishing this specific case from general divorce rules and emphasizing the unique sanctity of the Ihram state.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Al Hassan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one in Ihraam, when he marries while being in Ihraam, separation would be effected between the two of them. Then they would not (be able to) be married again, ever’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali from ibn Bukayr from Ibrahim ibn al-Hassan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
if one in the state of Ihram gets married, and he is still in the state of Ihram, they are separated and they can never marry each other again.’”
